extracted.intended_audience: general news audience interested in politics, culture, and media
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on a comedian's controversial on-air remark and the ensuing public, political, and corporate responses (apology, network statements, advertiser reactions, comparisons to other incidents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether a comedian's on-air use of vulgar or explicit terms is acceptable (the article: Bee used 'a vulgar term for the female anatomy' and TBS said 'Those words should not have been aired').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames such language as 'vile and inappropriate' and notes that it 'should not have been aired,' indicating a standard that broadcast content should avoid explicit profanity directed at individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that the performer acknowledge wrongdoing and apologize when a line has been crossed (Bee tweeted: 'I would like to sincerely apologize... It was inappropriate and inexcusable. I crossed a line, and I deeply regret it.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective response includes a clear statement of apology, an admission that a line was crossed, and expressed regret; networks may view apology as the 'right action.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Network responsibility and editorial oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility of the broadcaster to prevent airing inappropriate language and to own mistakes (TBS: 'It was our mistake too, and we regret it').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasters are expected to demonstrate that explicit profanity about members of an administration will not be condoned and to acknowledge institutional error when such content airs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences involving advertisers and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial and programming consequences for offensive remarks (article notes at least two advertisers 'have indicated they will pull their ads' and references calls to cancel Full Frontal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offensive on-air comments can lead to advertiser pullouts and public calls for cancellation; networks may face financial and reputational pressure to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative enforcement / perceived double standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of consistency in how networks and officials respond to controversial statements (Donald Trump tweeted: 'A total double standard...'), comparing treatment of different commentators and incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public and political actors may judge responses through the lens of consistency, highlighting perceived double standards when similar incidents receive different outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political reaction and public condemnation
rubrics_metrics.description: How political figures and administrations react to a comedian's remark (Press Secretary Sarah Sanders described the remarks as 'vile and vicious').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official condemnations frame the seriousness of a comment and can amplify calls for accountability; such responses shape public perception and institutional reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual comparison to prior incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Using past controversies (e.g., Roseanne Barr's racist tweet and subsequent show cancellation) as a benchmark for evaluating current incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons to past cases are used to argue for similar consequences or to illustrate differences in severity, context, or institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting female public figures with sexualized profanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular condemnation of explicit sexualized profanity directed at female members of an administration (Sanders: executives 'must demonstrate that such explicit profanity about female members of this administration will not be condoned').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights a norm that sexualized insults aimed at women in public life are especially unacceptable and demand organizational repudiation.
